speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe when the swelling in your right knee started and if you have experienced any recent trauma? Also, could you tell me more about your family history of similar joint problems?

speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the swelling come and go, or has it been constant, and have you noticed any bleeding issues like frequent nosebleeds or easy bruising? I would like to check his bleeding time and factor levels to see if this is hemophilia. REQUEST TEST: Coagulation Panel

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: ACT 52.0 s (prolonged), PT 14.0 s, Thrombin time < 2 seconds deviation from control

speaker: Doctor
text: The prolonged ACT with normal PT suggests a defect in the intrinsic pathway, likely hemophilia. To distinguish between Hemophilia A and B, I need to check the specific clotting factors. REQUEST TEST: Factor VIII and Factor IX levels

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal factor levels rule out typical hemophilia, so I need to consider other bleeding disorders. Does the patient have a history of bleeding from minor cuts, gum bleeding, or bleeding after vaccinations, and have you noticed any petechiae or purpura on his skin? REQUEST TEST: Platelet Function Assay

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal factor and platelet levels rule out hemophilia and platelet function disorders, so I suspect a factor XIII deficiency given the family history and spontaneous hemarthrosis. REQUEST TEST: Factor XIII Level

speaker: Doctor
text: With all standard coagulation tests normal, I suspect a structural or inflammatory cause rather than a bleeding disorder. Has the knee been warm or red to the touch, and does the child have a fever or refuse to bear weight on the leg? REQUEST TEST: Knee Ultrasound

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Compatible with hemarthrosis of the right knee, no evidence of fracture or dislocation.

speaker: Doctor
text: The ultrasound confirms hemarthrosis, yet standard coagulation screens are normal, which strongly suggests a rare bleeding disorder like Factor XIII deficiency that wasn't fully ruled out by the initial screen. To confirm this, I need to see the specific activity level of Factor XIII. REQUEST TEST: Factor XIII Activity Level

speaker: Doctor
text: Since standard coagulation screens and Factor XIII are normal, I need to rule out von Willebrand disease, which can present with hemarthrosis in severe cases. REQUEST TEST: von Willebrand Factor Antigen and Activity

speaker: Doctor
text: With all standard coagulation and von Willebrand tests normal, I must consider a rare clotting factor deficiency like Factor XI or a platelet adhesion disorder. Does the patient have a history of bleeding after circumcision or dental procedures, and has he experienced any excessive bleeding from minor cuts? REQUEST TEST: Factor XI Level

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the recurrent hemarthrosis with normal standard coagulation profiles and a family history, I suspect a rare platelet function defect or a mild factor deficiency not yet tested. DIAGNOSIS READY: Glanzmann's Thrombasthenia
